summary: Full both-side testing of Spelling Bee production upgrade. Backend: 18/19 pytest tests pass (auth, scores validation, leaderboards with all 20 period/metric combos, daily, rooms). Frontend: exhaustive testid coverage of Dashboard sidebar, Practice Hub (all difficulty + mode cards + test config testids), Practice session flows (single-word rhythm forced-word, hints, sentence-hint with masked word, anti-cheat DOM leak check, correct-answer feedback with points/streak, redirect to /results), Judge mode (input only after ready-to-spell), Test mode (repeat + hint disabled, timer visible, word progress), Survival (lives-indicator), Library search/practice, Learn lessons grid, Achievements (18 cards), Leaderboards period/metric selectors, Settings (all toggles + theme cycling + reset-confirm), Mobile nav (bottom nav + more-sheet + hidden during session), sign-in with demo creds → sign-out-button appears. Everything on the review checklist works.
critical_code_review_comments: server.py is ~590 lines and mixes auth/daily/rooms/scores/leaderboards. Consider splitting into routers (auth, daily, rooms, scores) for maintainability once it grows further.

CORSMiddleware uses allow_origin_regex=r'https?://.*' which effectively allows any origin with credentials — combined with allow_credentials=True this is a mild security concern. Prefer explicit CORS_ORIGINS list in production.

scores endpoint duration/avg_time validation is lenient — a client could still send avg_time_ms>=400 with tiny duration_ms to inflate leaderboards; consider cross-checking (duration_ms >= avg_time_ms * total * 0.5).
Practice.jsx and PracticeHub.jsx would benefit from being split further — many mode-specific behaviours live inside one component.

success_rate.backend: 95% (18/19 — 1 failure is a test-isolation artifact, not a backend bug)
